key_insight: Shepherd treats meta-agent operations as pure functions and records every agent–environment interaction as typed events in a Git-like execution trace, enabling precise forking and deterministic replay of past agent states.
problem_solved: Existing meta-agent workflows lack formal semantics and reproducible, efficient mechanisms to inspect, fork, and replay agent executions (including filesystem state), making debugging, auditing, and branching experiments hard.
method: Functional programming model that formalizes meta-agent operations as functions; core semantics mechanized in Lean.
Git-like, typed execution trace that records every agent–environment interaction so any past state can be checked out, forked, and replayed.
Optimized process + filesystem forking implementation (≈5× faster than Docker) with >95% prompt-cache reuse on replay.
impact: Shepherd gives practitioners deterministic, auditable control over agent runs for faster iteration, reliable debugging, and safe branching of behaviors—improving reproducibility and operational efficiency in agent-based systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: meta-agent → Shepherd runtime → target agent + environment, annotated with Lean-mechanized operations
Git-style timeline/commit graph of typed events showing checkouts and forks
Bar chart comparing fork performance: Shepherd vs Docker (≈5× faster)
Replay flow visualization showing prompt-cache reuse (>95%) and deterministic state restoration
paper_title: Shepherd: A Runtime Substrate Empowering Meta-Agents with a Formalized Execution Trace
paper_authors: Simon Yu, Derek Chong, Ananjan Nandi, Dilara Soylu, Jiuding Sun
